[Page 1]
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT — NOT A REAL AGREEMENT Page 1
FICTIONAL INDIAN SERVICE & FUNDING
AGREEMENT
12-page synthetic document for testing document-risk analysis software
IMPORTANT: This is an intentionally fictional test sample. All names, addresses, identification numbers, amounts, claims
and terms are invented. It is not legal advice and must not be signed or used as a real agreement.
Document ID: TEST-IN-2026-041
Purported date: 10 October 2026
Purported place: Bengaluru, Karnataka, India
Subject: Digital marketing, business support, data access and advance-payment arrangement.
This sample deliberately contains high-risk wording, vague obligations, inconsistent dates and amounts, missing
information, overbroad permissions, contradictory provisions and questionable legal assertions. These defects are
included so an analysis system can identify and explain them.
Parties named in this sample
Provider: Example Growth Solutions Private Limited, a fictional entity, stated to have an office at “12 Example
Road, Bengaluru”. No company registration number or verified address is supplied.
Customer: A fictional small business described only as “the Customer”. The Customer’s legal name, registered
address, authorised signatory and contact details are intentionally omitted.
The labels “High Risk”, “Medium Risk” and “Low Risk” in any analysis of this sample should be treated as software
outputs requiring human review, not as a court finding or legal conclusion.

[Page 2]
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT — NOT A REAL AGREEMENT Page 2
Scope of Work and Deliverables
1. Services
The Provider may provide online promotion, customer-list management, website updates, analytics reports,
business introductions and any other service that the Provider considers useful. The phrase “any other service” is
not limited by a written change request.
The Provider shall deliver “good results” within a reasonable period. No objective performance target, campaign
quantity, acceptance test, delivery schedule, support hours or named project owner is stated.
The Customer believes that the package includes 30 promotional posts per month. The Provider may instead deliver
up to 12 posts per month, or fewer if the Provider decides that market conditions are unsuitable. Both descriptions
are intended to apply.
2. Customer responsibilities
The Customer must provide all requested material within one day of a request, regardless of weekends, holidays,
availability or whether the request is relevant. If the Customer does not comply, the Provider may treat all remaining
work as completed.
The Provider may change the scope without written approval, and any resulting additional charge will be “fair and
customary”. No rate card, spending cap or approval process is attached.
3. Acceptance
All work is automatically accepted when sent by email, even if the email is not received, the attachment is corrupted,
or the Customer reports a defect. Elsewhere, the Customer is given 15 business days to review the same work. The
document does not explain which rule takes priority.

[Page 3]
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT — NOT A REAL AGREEMENT Page 3
Fees, Advance Payment and Refunds
4. Payment terms
The stated package fee is n1,20,000 plus applicable taxes. A separate schedule states that the total fee is
n1,80,000 inclusive of all taxes. The Provider may select whichever amount is more beneficial to it.
The Customer must pay an advance of n75,000 within 24 hours. A later paragraph says the advance is n50,000
and is due within seven calendar days. No signed quotation or invoice is attached.
Late payment attracts a charge of 8% per day, compounded daily, without a maximum limit. The Provider may also
add an administration charge of any amount it chooses. No method for calculating disputed invoices is provided.
5. Refunds
All payments are described as non-refundable under all circumstances. Another sentence promises a full refund if
the Provider delivers no work within 60 days. A third sentence says refunds are entirely at the Provider’s discretion
and may be paid as store credit only.
The Provider may retain the entire advance even if it cancels the project before starting. No deductions, evidence
requirements, refund timeline or dispute process are defined.
6. Taxes and bank details
The Customer must pay any taxes requested by the Provider, even if the tax type or calculation is not identified.
Payment instructions are stated to be “provided separately”; no verified account name, invoice number or payment
confirmation procedure is included.

[Page 4]
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT — NOT A REAL AGREEMENT Page 4
Duration, Renewal and Termination
7. Term
The agreement begins on 1 November 2026 and ends on 31 October 2026. It also states that the initial term lasts 12
months from the date of signature, which may be different from both dates.
Unless the Customer sends a cancellation request 90 days before the agreement begins, it renews automatically for
five years. The Provider may change renewal fees at any time, including retroactively.
8. Termination by Customer
The Customer may terminate for any reason by giving 180 days’ notice. Another clause states that the Customer
cannot terminate for any reason during the first five years. No rule explains the conflict.
If the Customer terminates, it must pay all future fees for the full renewal period, all projected profits and an
additional penalty determined by the Provider. No calculation or cap is specified.
9. Termination by Provider
The Provider may suspend or terminate the service immediately without notice, explanation or refund. The Provider
may also terminate only after giving 30 days’ written notice. No cure period is defined for either party.
Upon termination, the Provider may permanently delete all Customer files immediately, but another provision
requires it to retain all files for seven years. No priority rule, export format or handover period is provided.

[Page 5]
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT — NOT A REAL AGREEMENT Page 5
Risk Allocation and Indemnity
10. Disclaimer
The Provider does not guarantee any result, accuracy, availability, security, continuity or suitability of the service.
However, the sales description elsewhere promises “guaranteed growth and error-free delivery”. The document
does not define either phrase.
The Provider disclaims responsibility for all losses, including losses caused by its own negligence, mistakes,
unauthorised access, service interruption or failure to perform. The scope and enforceability of this wording require
qualified legal review.
11. Indemnity
The Customer must indemnify the Provider, its affiliates, employees, contractors, relatives, successors and any
person connected with them against every claim, cost, loss, fine or allegation, whether caused by the Customer or
not.
The Customer must pay the requested indemnity amount within two hours of receiving a message. No defence
procedure, notice requirement, proof of loss, mitigation duty or opportunity to dispute the claim is provided.
12. Liability cap
The Provider’s total liability is capped at n100, regardless of the amount paid. A later clause says the cap is
n10,000, while the sales schedule says the Provider accepts unlimited liability for all failures. No clause states which
provision overrides the others.

[Page 6]
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT — NOT A REAL AGREEMENT Page 6
Confidentiality and Personal Information
13. Confidential information
Each party must protect confidential information using reasonable care. However, the Provider may publish any
Customer information, screenshots, documents or messages for advertising whenever it considers publication
useful, without separate permission.
The agreement does not define confidential information, permitted recipients, security controls, breach notification
deadlines, return or deletion procedures, or exceptions for information already public or independently developed.
14. Personal data
The Customer may provide names, phone numbers, email addresses, customer purchase records and identity
documents. The Provider may copy, analyse, transfer, sell or share these materials with any third party for any
purpose and for an unlimited period.
No specific retention period, access-control policy, deletion process, security standard, data-processing instruction
or contact for privacy requests is supplied. The document asserts that consent is unnecessary in every situation,
without explaining the factual or legal basis.
This sample uses no real personal data. The broad permission language is deliberately included as a test case for
identifying privacy and confidentiality concerns.

[Page 7]
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT — NOT A REAL AGREEMENT Page 7
Intellectual Property and Use Rights
15. Ownership
All deliverables, including designs, copy, reports and source files, belong exclusively to the Provider forever. A
separate paragraph says ownership transfers to the Customer immediately after the first payment. Another says
ownership transfers only after full payment and written confirmation.
The Provider may reuse the Customer’s logo, confidential campaign strategy and unpublished materials for any
other client. The Customer receives a “worldwide, permanent, revocable, non-exclusive and exclusive” licence;
these descriptors conflict and are not clarified.
16. Third-party materials
The Provider may include third-party images, fonts, music, software or datasets without identifying the source or
confirming the licence. The Customer is responsible for every resulting claim even if it had no control over the
selection.
No process exists for reporting suspected infringement, replacing disputed content, transferring editable files or
confirming whether open-source licence conditions have been met.
17. Credentials
The Customer must share administrator passwords in plain text through any messaging service requested by the
Provider. The agreement contains no multi-factor authentication requirement, access expiry, credential rotation or
access log obligation.

[Page 8]
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT — NOT A REAL AGREEMENT Page 8
Representations, Compliance and Dubious Claims
18. Statements by the parties
The Provider represents that it is “fully approved by every Indian government department” and that the agreement
“cannot be challenged in any court”. No approval number, issuing authority, supporting certificate or legal source is
identified.
The Customer is deemed to confirm that all supplied information is accurate even if the Provider fills in missing
information or edits the Customer’s documents without review. No verification process is described.
19. Compliance
Each party shall comply with applicable law. At the same time, the Provider may ignore any legal notice or regulator
request if responding would delay its work. The document does not identify a compliance owner or process for
handling lawful requests.
A clause states that a verbal promise always overrides this written agreement, while another says that only signed
written amendments are valid. This is a deliberate inconsistency for analysis.
20. No verification evidence
No certificate of incorporation, GST details, authorisation letter, signed statement of work, proof of address or
identity verification is attached. This absence does not by itself prove fraud, but it is a verification gap that should be
flagged.

[Page 9]
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT — NOT A REAL AGREEMENT Page 9
Disputes, Governing Law and Notices
21. Governing law
The agreement is said to be governed by Indian law and, in another paragraph, exclusively by the laws of an
unnamed foreign country. The document does not resolve the conflict or explain the connection to that country.
22. Courts and arbitration
Any dispute must be filed only in Bengaluru. Another clause requires exclusive jurisdiction in New Delhi. A third
requires arbitration in “the Provider’s preferred location”, which may be changed after a dispute begins.
The arbitration clause does not identify the seat, language, appointment procedure, number of arbitrators or rules. It

risks.reason: भारतीय संविदा अधिनियम की धारा 74 के अंतर्गत वास्तविक नुकसान की तुलना में अधिक निश्चित जुर्माना, सुरक्षा जमा जब्ती या उच्च ब्याज दर लागू करता है।
risks.simpleExplanation: यह शर्त पैसे या सुरक्षा जमा को जब्त करने या देरी पर भारी जुर्माना लगाने की अनुमति देती है। सुनिश्चित करें कि दंड केवल प्रमाणित वास्तविक नुकसान तक ही सीमित हो।

risks.title: व्यापक क्षतिपूर्ति और असीमित वित्तीय दायित्व जोखिम (Uncapped Liability)
risks.reason: बिना किसी अधिकतम वित्तीय सीमा (Liability Cap) के व्यापक नुकसान, तीसरे पक्ष के दावों और अप्रत्यक्ष हानियों के लिए भारी वित्तीय जिम्मेदारी तय करता है।
risks.simpleExplanation: आपको बिना किसी अधिकतम सीमा के बड़े नुकसान या कानूनी दावों का भुगतान करना पड़ सकता है। अनुबंध शुल्क से जुड़ी एक उचित देयता सीमा (Liability Cap) तय करें।

risks.title: बिना पूर्व सूचना के एकतरफा निर्णय या अनुबंध समाप्त करने का अधिकार
risks.reason: यह प्रावधान एक पक्ष को बिना किसी पूर्व सूचना या वैध कारण के शर्तों को बदलने या अनुबंध को समाप्त करने की असमान शक्ति देता है।
risks.simpleExplanation: एक पक्ष अपने आप तुरंत निर्णय ले सकता है या अनुबंध समाप्त कर सकता है। दोनों पक्षों के लिए समान नोटिस अवधि और निष्पक्ष मानदंड जोड़ने की मांग करें।

documentChecks.recommendation: अप्रत्याशित घटनाओं की परिभाषा, सूचना समय-सीमा और 30–60 दिनों से अधिक व्यवधान होने पर समाप्ति अधिकार सहित एक मानक Force Majeure खंड शामिल करें।

Assignment Question 4: Parsing PDF Files
Python Program to Extract Revenue, Profit, and Expenses
Install the required library before running the program:
pip install pdfminer.six
Python Code
from pdfminer.high_level import extract_text
import re
# Extract text from the PDF file
text = extract_text("annual_report.pdf")
# Financial terms to search
terms = ["Revenue", "Profit", "Expenses"]
# Store the extracted values
report = {}
for term in terms:
pattern = (
rf"{term}\\s*[:\\-]?\\s*"
rf"(?:Rs\\.?|INR|\\$)?\\s*"
rf"([\\d,]+(?:\\.\\d+)?)"
)
match = re.search(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE)
if match:
report[term] = match.group(1)
else:
report[term] = "Not found"
# Display the structured report
print("Financial Report")
for term, value in report.items():
print(term, ":", value)

Profit : 120000
Expenses : 380000
Note: Keep annual_report.pdf in the same folder as the Python script. The output values above are
examples; the actual values depend on the PDF content. This pattern works best when each financial
keyword is followed by its value. Scanned PDFs may require OCR, and complex tables may need extra
processing.

Assignment Question 4: Parsing PDF Files
Python Program to Extract Revenue, Profit, and Expenses
Install the required library before running the program:
pip install pdfminer.six
Python Code
from pdfminer.high_level import extract_text
import re
# Extract text from the PDF file
text = extract_text("annual_report.pdf")
# Financial terms to search
terms = ["Revenue", "Profit", "Expenses"]
# Store the extracted values
report = {}
for term in terms:
pattern = (
rf"{term}\\s*[:\\-]?\\s*"
rf"(?:Rs\\.?|INR|\\$)?\\s*"
rf"([\\d,]+(?:\\.\\d+)?)"
)
match = re.search(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE)
if match:
report[term] = match.group(1)
else:
report[term] = "Not found"
# Display the structured report
print("Financial Report")
for term, value in report.items():
print(term, ":", value)
Sample Output

Revenue : 500000
Profit : 120000
Expenses : 380000
Note: Keep annual_report.pdf in the same folder as the Python script. The output values above are
examples; the actual values depend on the PDF content. This pattern works best when each financial
keyword is followed by its value. Scanned PDFs may require OCR, and complex tables may need extra
processing.
References
1. pdfminer.six Documentation: https://pdfminersix.readthedocs.io/
2. Python Regular Expression Documentation: https://docs.python.org/3/library/re.html

This Rental Agreement is made between Mr. Rajesh Kumar, hereinafter referred to as the Landlord,

The Tenant shall be responsible for electricity, water and other utility charges. The Landlord shall be
responsible for major structural repairs.

Either party may terminate this agreement by providing 30 days' notice to the other party.
6. Property Use
The property shall be used only for residential purposes. The Tenant shall not use the property for any
illegal activity.
7. Subletting
The Tenant shall not sublet the property to another person without permission from the Landlord.
8. Disputes
Any dispute arising from this agreement shall be resolved according to the applicable laws.

commonRisks: Post-termination non-compete restrictions (void under Section 27 of Indian Contract Act, 1872)
Unilateral termination without notice or severance pay
Excessive training bond or liquidated damages penalty
Broad intellectual property claims over personal off-hours work
Schemes.regulatoryFramework: Indian Contract Act, 1872 & Shops and Establishments Act

Schemes.name: Residential & Commercial Lease / Rental Agreement
Schemes.description: Verification framework for rental agreements, security deposit refund timelines, lock-in periods, maintenance liability, and eviction notice.
commonRisks: Arbitrary security deposit forfeiture without itemized proof of damage
Unannounced landlord entry without 24-hour prior notice
One-sided lock-in period binding only the tenant
Schemes.regulatoryFramework: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 & Model Tenancy Act

Schemes.name: Mutual & Unilateral Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA)
Schemes.description: Standard benchmark for evaluating confidentiality scope, exclusions from confidential information, survival period, and injunctive relief.
commonRisks: Perpetual/indefinite confidentiality obligation with no time limit
Missing exclusions for independently developed or publicly available information
Pre-estimated liquidated damages disproportionate to actual breach
Foreign or inconvenient governing law and arbitration venue
Schemes.regulatoryFramework: Indian Contract Act, 1872 & Information Technology Act, 2000

Schemes.name: Master Services Agreement (MSA) & SaaS Vendor Contract
